### Radical-cure treatment by G6PD status

| G6PD category | Radical-cure treatment policy | Treatment implementation | Implementation details | Health-system level | Health-system details | Implementation year | Additional safety recommendations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G6PD normal: > 70% enzyme activity** | TQ or high-dose 7-day PQ | Partially implemented | Implemented where G6PD testing is available | _Not reported_ | _Not reported_ | 2025 | Counselling for adverse events |
| **G6PD normal: no definition** | PQ 0.25 mg/kg/day over 14 days or PQ 0.5 mg/kg/day over 7 days if adherence is expected to be low and a risk-benefit analysis is conducted | Partially implemented | Implemented where G6PD testing is available | _Not reported_ | _Not reported_ | 2006 | Counselling for adverse events |
| **G6PD deficient: < 30% enzyme activity** | PQ 0.75 mg/kg/week weekly for 8 weeks | Partially implemented | Implemented where G6PD testing is available | _Not reported_ | _Not reported_ | _Not reported_ | Not specified |
| **If no testing available** | PQ 0.25 mg/kg/day over 14 days or PQ 0.5 mg/kg/day over 7 days if adherence is expected to be low and a risk-benefit analysis is conducted | Implemented | _Not reported_ | _Not reported_ | _Not reported_ | 2006 | Not specified |
:::

### Radical-cure follow-up by G6PD status

| G6PD category | Follow-up approach | Follow-up implementation | Follow-up implementation year |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G6PD normal: > 70% enzyme activity** | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented | _Not reported_ |
| **G6PD normal: no definition** | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented | _Not reported_ |
| **G6PD deficient: < 30% enzyme activity** | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented | _Not reported_ |
| **If no testing available** | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented | _Not reported_ |

### Country-specific policy context

<div class="country-policy-context"><p>Costa Rica has implemented tafenoquine, being the first country in Central America and the Carribbean implementing tafenoquine. Tafenoquine is the first choice for treatment of G6PD normal individuals. If not available use of PQ high dose If G6PD testing is not available, healthcare providers can refer the patient to a health facility that has testing as long as testing and treatment can be within 24hrs.</p></div>
